en.title: DHS Proposes $70,000 Initial and $30,000 Subsequent Fees for F-1 OPT
en.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has filed a proposed rule that would create new fees for Optional Practical Training (OPT) under the F-1 student visa program. The rule would require a $70,000 fee for initial OPT and a $30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT period, applying to each F-1 student at a SEVP-certified institution.
points: This is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), part of DHS, and is not yet final or in effect.
The proposed fee is $70,000 for initial OPT and $30,000 for any subsequent OPT, per F-1 nonimmigrant student.
The fee would be paid by the SEVP-certified school, not the student, before a designated school official recommends the student for OPT.
DHS states the goal is to combat fraud, strengthen immigration system integrity and protect U.S. workers.

The comment period runs 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, with a separate 60 day comment period for the related information collection; the rule is scheduled for publication on October 8, 2026, so these periods would run from that date.
Comments must be submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov under Docket No. ICEB-2026-0100; comments sent by email, mail, or other channels will not be considered.
en.who: F-1 international students seeking or currently on Optional Practical Training, and SEVP-certified schools and employers involved in OPT.
en.action: Those wishing to comment should submit remarks through regulations.gov referencing Docket No. ICEB-2026-0100 before the comment deadline, and monitor the Federal Register for the final published version and exact deadlines.

ko.title: DHS, F-1 OPT에 최초 7만 달러, 재OPT 3만 달러 수수료 신설 제안
ko.summary: 미국 국토안보부(DHS)가 F-1 학생비자 소지자의 선택적 실무연수(OPT)에 신규 수수료를 부과하는 규칙제정안을 연방관보 공개열람에 제출했습니다. 이 제안에 따르면 최초 OPT에는 7만 달러, 이후 재OPT에는 3만 달러의 수수료가 각 F-1 학생마다 부과됩니다.
points: 이번 규칙은 국토안보부 산하 미국 이민세관단속국(ICE)이 발표한 규칙제정안(NPRM)으로, 아직 확정되거나 시행된 것이 아닙니다.
SEVP 인증 기관에서 공부하는 F-1 학생 1인당 최초 OPT 수수료는 7만 달러, 재OPT 수수료는 3만 달러로 제안되었습니다.
수수료는 학생이 아니라 SEVP 인증 학교가 부담하며, 학교의 DSO가 SEVIS에서 OPT를 추천하기 전에 납부해야 합니다.
DHS는 사기 방지, 이민 제도의 신뢰성 강화, 미국 근로자 보호를 목적으로 제시했습니다.
의견수렴 기간은 연방관보 게재일로부터 30일이며, 관련 정보수집 항목에 대해서는 별도로 60일의 의견수렴 기간이 적용됩니다. 이 규칙은 2026년 10월 8일 게재 예정이므로 해당 기간은 그 날짜부터 계산됩니다.
의견은 regulations.gov의 연방 전자규칙제정 포털을 통해 문서번호 ICEB-2026-0100으로 제출해야 하며, 이메일이나 우편 등 다른 방식으로 제출된 의견은 접수되지 않습니다.
ko.who: OPT를 신청하거나 현재 OPT 상태인 F-1 유학생, 그리고 OPT와 관련된 SEVP 인증 교육기관 및 고용주가 영향을 받습니다.
ko.action: 의견을 제출하려는 경우 regulations.gov에서 문서번호 ICEB-2026-0100을 참조하여 의견수렴 마감일 전에 제출해야 하며, 최종 확정 내용과 정확한 마감일은 연방관보 정식 게재본을 통해 확인해야 합니다.

es.title: DHS propone tarifas de 70,000 y 30,000 dólares para el OPT de estudiantes F-1
es.summary: El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) presentó una propuesta de regla que crearía nuevas tarifas para el Entrenamiento Práctico Opcional (OPT) bajo la visa de estudiante F-1. La propuesta establecería una tarifa de 70,000 dólares para el OPT inicial y 30,000 dólares para cualquier OPT posterior, por cada estudiante F-1 en una institución certificada por SEVP.
points: Se trata de un Aviso de Propuesta de Reglamentación (NPRM) del Servicio de Control de Inmigración y Aduanas (ICE), dependencia del DHS, y todavía no es una regla final ni está en vigor.
La tarifa propuesta es de 70,000 dólares para el OPT inicial y 30,000 dólares para cualquier OPT subsiguiente, por estudiante no inmigrante F-1.
La tarifa la pagaría la escuela certificada por SEVP, no el estudiante, antes de que el funcionario escolar designado (DSO) recomiende al estudiante para OPT.
El DHS afirma que el objetivo es combatir el fraude, fortalecer la integridad del sistema migratorio y proteger a los trabajadores estadounidenses.

El período de comentarios públicos es de 30 días después de la publicación en el Federal Register, con un período separado de 60 días para comentarios sobre la recopilación de información relacionada; la regla está programada para publicarse el 8 de octubre de 2026, por lo que estos plazos correrían a partir de esa fecha.

Los comentarios deben enviarse a través del Portal Federal de Reglamentación Electrónica en regulations.gov, bajo el número de expediente ICEB-2026-0100; los comentarios enviados por correo electrónico, correo postal u otros medios no serán considerados.
es.who: Estudiantes internacionales con visa F-1 que buscan o actualmente tienen Entrenamiento Práctico Opcional, así como las instituciones certificadas por SEVP y los empleadores involucrados en el OPT.
es.action: Quienes deseen comentar deben enviar sus observaciones a través de regulations.gov citando el número de expediente ICEB-2026-0100 antes del plazo de comentarios, y revisar el Federal Register para conocer la versión final publicada y los plazos exactos.

zh.title: DHS提议对F-1学生OPT征收初次7万美元、后续3万美元费用
zh.summary: 美国国土安全部(DHS)已提交一项拟议规则,将为F-1学生签证项下的选择性实习训练(OPT)设立新收费。根据该提案,每名在SEVP认证院校就读的F-1学生,首次OPT将收取7万美元,后续OPT收取3万美元。
points: 该文件为美国移民及海关执法局(ICE,隶属国土安全部)发布的拟议规则制定通知(NPRM),目前尚未成为正式生效规定。
拟议费用为每名F-1非移民学生首次OPT收取7万美元,任何后续OPT收取3万美元。
该费用将由 SEVP 认证学校而非学生本人缴纳，须在指定学校官员（DSO）推荐学生申请 OPT 之前缴清。
国土安全部表示,此举旨在打击欺诈、加强移民体系的公信力并保护美国工人。
公众意见征询期为在联邦公报刊登后30天内,针对相关信息收集事项另设60天意见征询期;该规则预计于2026年10月8日刊登,相关期限将从该日起计算。
意见须通过regulations.gov的联邦电子立法门户提交,并注明案卷编号ICEB-2026-0100,通过电子邮件、邮寄等其他方式提交的意见将不被受理。
zh.who: 正在申请或已处于OPT阶段的F-1国际学生,以及参与OPT的SEVP认证院校和雇主。
zh.action: 希望提交意见者应在截止日期前通过regulations.gov提交意见并注明案卷编号ICEB-2026-0100,并关注联邦公报正式刊登版本以获取准确截止日期。

ja.title: DHS、F-1 OPTに初回7万ドル、更新時3万ドルの手数料新設を提案
ja.summary: 米国国土安全保障省(DHS)は、F-1学生ビザ制度に基づくオプショナル・プラクティカル・トレーニング(OPT)に新たな手数料を設ける規則案を連邦官報の公開閲覧に提出しました。提案では、SEVP認定機関に在籍するF-1学生1人につき、初回OPTで7万ドル、以降のOPTで3万ドルの手数料が課されます。
points: 本案はDHS傘下の米国移民関税執行局(ICE)による規則制定案(NPRM)であり、まだ最終確定しておらず施行もされていません。
提案されている手数料は、F-1非移民学生1人あたり初回OPTで7万ドル、以降の各OPTで3万ドルです。
手数料は学生ではなく SEVP 認定校が負担し、指定学校職員（DSO）が OPT を推薦する前に納付する必要があります。
DHSは、不正行為への対処、移民制度の信頼性強化、米国人労働者の保護を目的として挙げています。
意見募集期間は連邦官報掲載日から30日間で、関連する情報収集事項については別途60日間の意見募集期間が設けられます。本規則は2026年10月8日に掲載予定であり、各期間はその日から起算されます。
意見はregulations.govの連邦電子規則制定ポータルを通じて、案件番号ICEB-2026-0100を明記のうえ提出する必要があり、電子メールや郵送など他の方法による意見は受理されません。
ja.who: OPTを申請中または現在OPT中のF-1留学生、およびOPTに関わるSEVP認定教育機関と雇用主が対象です。
ja.action: 意見を提出したい場合は、意見募集期限までにregulations.govで案件番号ICEB-2026-0100を参照して提出し、正式な連邦官報掲載版で最終内容と正確な期限を確認してください。

Department of Homeland Security

[DHS Docket No. ICEB-2026-0100]

( printed page 64566)
AGENCY:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
ACTION:
Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
SUMMARY:

This rule proposes new fees for Optional Practical Training (OPT) to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect U.S. workers. The following fees would apply for each F-1 nonimmigrant student to engage in OPT through a Student and Exchange Visitor Program-certified institution: $70,000 for initial OPT; and $30,000 for any subsequent OPT.
DATES:

Comments must be received on or before November 9, 2026. Information collection comment period: Comments on the information collection described in the Paperwork Reduction Act section below must be received by December 7, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments on the entirety of this rule, which must be identified by Docket No. ICEB-2026-0100, through the following method:
Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. Follow the website instructions to submit comments.

Comments on the information collection may be submitted to the same docket as the NPRM or as described in the “submitting comments” section below. In addition, all comments on the information collection must include the OMB Control Number in the body of the comments.

Comments submitted in a manner other than the Federal eRulemaking Portal, including emails or letters sent to the Department of Homeland Security (the Department or DHS), will not be considered comments, and will not receive a response from DHS. Please note that DHS cannot accept any hand delivered or couriered comments, nor any comments contained on any form of digital media storage devices, such as CDs, DVDs, and USB drives. If you cannot submit your material using https://www.regulations.gov, contact the office in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section of this document for alternate instructions.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:

Office of the Principal Legal Advisor, Regulatory Affairs Unit, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Department of Homeland Security, 500 12th Street SW, Washington, DC 20536-5901. Telephone 202-732-6960 (not a toll-free number) (for questions only—no comments will be accepted at this phone number).
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Public Participation

DHS encourages all interested parties to participate in this rulemaking by submitting data, views, comments, and arguments on all aspects of this notice of proposed rulemaking. Comments providing the most assistance to DHS will reference a specific portion of this rule, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include the data, information, or authority that supports the recommended change. See the ADDRESSES section above for information on where to submit comments.
A. Submitting Comments

All comments must be submitted in English, or an English translation must be provided. If you submit comments, you must include the DHS docket number for this rulemaking (ICEB-2026-0100), indicate the specific section of this document to which each comment applies, and provide a reason for each suggestion or recommendation. Include data, information, or authority that supports the comment. Your comments must be submitted online by 11:59 p.m. ET of the last day of the comment period.

Instructions: To submit your comments online, go to https://www.regulations.gov and insert “ICEB-2026-0100” in the “Search” box. Click on the rule that appears in the “Search Results.” Click on the “Comment” box under the name of the rule and input your comments in the text box provided. When you are satisfied with your comments, follow the prompts, and then click “Submit Comment.”

Collection of information. You must submit comments on the collection of information discussed in this notice of proposed rulemaking to either DHS's docket or the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA). OIRA will have access to and view the comments submitted in the docket. OIRA submissions can also be sent using any of the following alternative methods:
Email (alternative): dhsdeskofficer@omb.eop.gov (include the docket number and “Attention: Desk Officer for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, DHS” in the subject line of the email).
Mail: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, Office of Management and Budget, 725 17th Street NW, Washington, DC 20503; Attention: Desk Officer, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, DHS.

DHS will post your comments to the federal e-Rulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov and will include any personal information you provide. Therefore, submitting this information makes it public. You may wish to consider limiting the amount of personal information that you provide in any voluntary public comment submission. DHS may withhold from public viewing information provided in comments that it determines is offensive or is otherwise deemed inappropriate for posting. For more information, please read the “Privacy & Security Notice” via the link in the footer of https://www.regulations.gov. DHS will consider all comments and materials received during the comment period and may change this rule based on your comments.
B. Viewing Comments and Documents

To view comments, as well as documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to https://www.regulations.gov and insert “ICEB-2026-0100” in the “Search” box. Click on the “Open Docket Folder,” then click on “View Comment” or “View All” under the “Comments” section of the page. Individuals without internet access can make alternate arrangements for viewing comments and documents related to this rulemaking by contacting the person listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section above. You may also sign up for email alerts on the online docket to be notified when comments are posted, or a final rule is published.

You may consider limiting the amount of personal information that you provide in your voluntary public comment submission because anyone can electronically search comments received in any of DHS's dockets by the name of the individual submitting the comment (or signing the comment, if submitted on behalf of an association, business, labor union, etc.).
